summary: Reading edition = the Weekly Shonen Jump serialization of Shimabukuro's Toriko: 396 chapters titled 'Gourmet N!!' in 43 tankobon (Gourmet 396 'Yet-Unseen Ingredients!!', 2016-11-21). That is the space AniList counts (396), the space toriko.fandom's Gourmet N pages use, and the space our 129 stored anchors sit in. Flag #695 is NOT an edition split: MangaUpdates' own record for the same work reads '43 Volumes (Complete)' and pins the anime coverage as 'Vol 1, Chap 1' - 'Vol 29, Chap 263', i.e. the identical numbering (v29 = chs 254-263). MU's latest_chapter=2 is a release-index artifact - the licensed title has only three surviving release rows on MU (v29.5, v1 c2, v1 c1), so the highest chapter among them is 2; it is not a chapter count and not a second edition (G37). Rows 141-144 adapt chs 233-253 in running order. The honest terminal is ep 146: its Gourmet-World half is Gourmet 254 'A Sad End!!' beat for beat - Ichiryu wounded by Hungry Space, his secret technique (All-Meal King-Eating Chopsticks) failing, both brothers' tears of parting, Midora's finishing blow, and the Meteor Spice fired at the Human World - per Toei Animation's own kakuwa arasuji for ep 146, matched against the fandom Gourmet 254 page. Ep 145 carries NO manga position at all: Toei's official synopsis for it is the Four Kings' anime-only combination attacks on Joie (Tornado Leg Boomerang is flagged 'only seen on the anime') plus Jiro/Setsuno subduing the brainwashed Teppei, none of which happens in chs 244-254 - so it is anchor_hostile under A44 and a filler candidate under T28. Ep 147 is the studio ending (A1, no anchor): Toriko defeats Joie, Ichiryu SURVIVES, and the Kings leave for the Gourmet World separately - all contradicting the manga. Post-series continue = ch 255; chs 255-396 (the manga's real ending of the Cooking Festival, Ichiryu's death, and the entire Gourmet World / Billion Bird / GOD half from ch 264) are never animated, and ch 245 is skipped outright. MU's 'Chap 263' pin is therefore OVERSTATED by nine chapters - right volume, wrong chapter - and it lands on filler rows 145-147, which is why G36 refuses it.

anchors.note: A4/A10: Komatsu's cry reviving Toriko (Gourmet 233 'Call!!'), Aimaru's Ultimate Routine (234-235), Starjun drawing the Burner Knife (236 'The Mightiest Rival!!') - Toei's official synopsis follows the four chapters in order; fandom episode field agrees. Re-affirms the stored anchor.

A4: Toriko vs Starjun's climax (237-239), Joie's entrance and the Nitro minions (241 'Mastermind!!'), Setsuno recognising the Cinderella knife and Jiro arriving to save her from a Nitro (242 'The Mystery Man, Joie!!') - the Toei synopsis ends exactly on Jiro's arrival, which is 242's close. Re-affirms the stored anchor.

A4: the visible body is 243 (Jiro's finger-flick, Grand Knocking, unmasking Joie as Froese's double) and 244 (the Rising Wolf Guinness Punch erased by Satan Mince, Joie's counterattack). The 246-247 tail is toriko.fandom's episode field only - Toei's synopsis for ep 143 does not mention the Gourmet World, but Toei's ep-144 synopsis RECAPS 'and meanwhile in the Gourmet World the Ichiryu-Midora duel was about to begin', which is consistent with a short 246/247 tag scene closing ep 143. Kept as stored; the tail is the weaker half. Ch 245 remains unadapted (existing annotation).

anchors.chapters_adapted: 248-253 (248-250 heavily compressed; the Hungry Space wound is replayed after the 251-253 flashback)
anchors.note: A4: the episode's canon spine is the Acacia/Froese/Midora flashback - the orphan Midora fed by Froese, Acacia and Froese leaving for GOD, Froese returning weakened, Midora fetching the Cure Water, Froese's death - which is Gourmet 251-253 exactly (Toei synopsis paras 2-3). The present-day duel material of 248-250 is only glimpsed (Toei shows the duel starting and then Ichiryu shredded by Hungry Space, a 249-250 technique), so START 248 rests on the fandom episode field alone; if Sean prefers the tighter read the START is 251. END 253 is firm - the flashback's end is 253's end.

anchors.chapters_adapted: 254 (abridged; the Ichiryu-Midora conclusion and the Meteor Spice launch)
anchors.note: THE HONEST TERMINAL (G56). Toei's official ep-146 synopsis, para 2: Ichiryu badly wounded by Midora's Hungry Space, releasing his secret technique for a direct hit that still fails to beat Midora, falling to the counterattack, tears of parting in both brothers' eyes, Midora's fist coming down, and the Meteor Spice fired at the Human World. That is Gourmet 254 'A Sad End!!' end to end (fandom's 254 page lists exactly Hungry Space, All-Meal King-Eating Chopsticks, the shared tears, the final blow and Meteor Spice). The episode's other half - Toriko's Gourmet-Cell rampage, Komatsu's cry, Toriko overpowering Joie - is anime-original, which is why the row is mixed. REPAIR of the stored 253: toriko.fandom's ep-145 AND ep-146 chapter fields both print '253' after ep 144's '248-253', the classic reading-position plateau, and AFG's 'ep 146 = ch 253' restates the same community figure; ch 253 is wholly the Froese flashback, which is in ep 144, not 146.

continue_points.note: After ep 144 you have seen through the end of Gourmet 253 (Froese's death). Ep 145 carries no manga position, and the next manga content on screen is ch 254 in ep 146 - so resume at 254. C2 parity with the anime.

C5, coverage + 1. Ep 146 is the last episode with any manga in it and it ends on ch 254's final beat (Meteor Spice fired), so read on from Gourmet 255 'Awakening!!'. Everything from 255 to the final chapter 396 is never animated - Midora sparing Ichiryu, Ichiryu's death at the hands of a Blue Nitro, the Human World's food collapse, and the whole second half of the manga (the Gourmet World from ch 264 on). Note also that ch 245, the manga's real close of the Cooking Festival (Starjun's Bloom and Midora's attack scattering NEO and the Bishokukai), is skipped by the anime, and the anime's own last three episodes replace the manga's ending outright - Toriko never defeats Joie in the manga and Komatsu stays kidnapped - so a reader who wants the manga's continuity intact can pick up from ch 245 instead.

anchor_hostile.why: A44 position-less. Toei's official synopsis for ep 145 is, in order: the Four Heavenly Kings' anime-only combination attacks on Joie (Super Voice Fry-turner, Machine Gun Sound Poison, Tornado Leg Boomerang - toriko.fandom's Toriko/Abilities entry for Tornado Leg Boomerang reads 'It was only seen on the anime'), Jiro and Setsuno fighting and sealing the Taste-Changed Teppei with Knocking, Joie's Gourmet-Eclipse pitch to Komatsu, and the Kings' combined ultimate technique. None of this occurs in Gourmet 244-254: in the manga Starjun refuses to hand Komatsu over, Blooms, and Midora's attack ends the festival (245), and Teppei stays with NEO (256). The stored anchor 253 [253] {253 (partial)} cannot stand - ch 253 is the Froese-death flashback, animated in ep 144, and no page of it is in ep 145. There is also no Gourmet-World segment in ep 145 (Toei describes one in 144 and in 146, none here). Type repair proposed separately.

annotations.note: The present-day Ichiryu vs Midora duel (Hungry Tongue, Minority World, the Emperor's Ring) is compressed almost out of the episode in favour of the 251-253 flashback; toriko.fandom's Ichiryu page states the anime's version of the fight 'were significantly shorter and provided less information about their past'.

Gourmet 254 is adapted with its outcome changed: in the anime Ichiryu's secret technique lands (it is dodged in the manga) and Midora does not kill him - toriko.fandom's Ichiryu page: 'the most important change in the story is that in the anime, Ichiryu still lives'. The episode's stadium half (Toriko's Gourmet-Cell rampage, Komatsu's cry, Toriko overpowering Joie) is anime-original, which is what makes the row mixed.

T28 mandatory tie on a filler row: the studio ending restages three manga beats without adapting their pages - Midora sparing Ichiryu (255), the Meteor Spice fallout and the IGO's emergency food relief (255/257), and Toriko and Komatsu setting out for the Gourmet World (264 'Now, to Gourmet World!!'). Every one is contradicted in substance: Ichiryu is alive and reconciles over Komatsu's soup, the Kings depart separately, and toriko.fandom's Meteor Spice page notes the attack 'was stopped by Toriko and the others' in the anime, 'preventing Midora from ending the Gourmet Age'. No anchor (A1).

repairs.why: Ep 146's Gourmet-World half is Gourmet 254 'A Sad End!!' in full (Hungry Space wound, the secret technique, the shared tears, the final blow, Meteor Spice fired at the Human World) per Toei Animation's official per-episode synopsis matched to the fandom chapter page. The stored 253 comes from a plateaued fandom episode field (144 '248-253', 145 '253', 146 '253') and from AFG restating the same community figure; ch 253 is the Froese flashback, which is ep 144's content. This contradicts the stored ruling of 2026-08-24 ('the honest terminal anchor is ep 146 -> ch 253') and is offered as an explicit repair, not an override.
Same evidence; ep 146's only manga content is ch 254, so START = END = 254.

repairs.new: 254 (abridged; the Ichiryu-Midora conclusion and the Meteor Spice launch)

repairs.why: Ch 254 is the first chapter of volume 29 (v29 = 254-263).
C5: furthest first-time coverage (254) + 1. Ch 255 'Awakening!!' opens on the aftermath the anime never shows.

A44/A1: ep 145 contains no manga pages at all - its whole plot (the Kings' anime-only combination attacks on Joie, Jiro/Setsuno sealing the Taste-Changed Teppei) has no counterpart in Gourmet 244-254, and ch 253's pages are in ep 144. Delete the anchor rather than leave a chapter number the reader cannot verify.
Follows the anchor deletion; with no position on the row there is nothing for the continue to hang on. Ep 144's continue (254) already carries the reader across ep 145.
The stored 253/parity assumed ep 145 finishes ch 253. It does not - ep 145 has no manga content - so after ep 144 the reader resumes at 254, which is also ep 146's START (C2 parity holds).

type_corrections.note: T28: the episode's whole job is an anime-original battle. Toei's official synopsis lists only the Four Kings' combination attacks on Joie (Tornado Leg Boomerang is documented on toriko.fandom as 'only seen on the anime'), Jiro and Setsuno sealing the brainwashed Teppei, and Joie's Gourmet-Eclipse speech to Komatsu - none of it in chs 244-254, where Starjun instead refuses Joie, Blooms, and Midora's attack ends the festival (ch 245), and Teppei stays with NEO (ch 256). toriko.fandom's ep-143 differences list already says 'all the events after Joie uses her Satan Mince technique are heavily altered and are not based on the manga', and ja-WP's Toriko article says the anime's endgame 'is original and differs from the source'. AFL types 145 canon, but as part of a 132-145 block; the stored type came from that block. Sean's call - the anchor deletion above stands either way (A44).

LOWER PRIORITY, judgment call - flagged rather than urged. Ep 144 is half canon (the Gourmet 251-253 Acacia/Froese/Midora flashback) and half anime-original (Toriko and Starjun returning to fight Joie, the Four Kings assembling; in the manga Toriko is unconscious and Terry finds him collapsed - ch 245). Both halves carry the episode's plot, which is the T27/T28 shape of mixed. AFL and the stored row say canon. Nothing about the anchor changes if this is declined - mixed rows keep anchors.

structure.notes: EDITION (flag #695) - resolved, and it is not an edition split. One reading edition exists: the Weekly Shonen Jump serialization, chapters titled 'Gourmet N!!' (グルメN), 1-396, collected in 43 tankobon; Gourmet 396 'Yet-Unseen Ingredients!!' ran 2016-11-21 and Gourmet 397 does not exist. AniList's 396 is that count; toriko.fandom's Chapter_N pages all redirect to Gourmet_N in the same space; our 129 stored anchors and the context's 43 volume boundaries are in it too. MangaUpdates is ALSO in that space - its record reads 'Status in Country of Origin: 43 Volumes (Complete)' and its Anime Start/End field reads 'Starts at Vol 1, Chap 1 / Ends at Vol 29, Chap 263 (with some differences)', and v29 = chs 254-263 matches our boundaries exactly. What MU's latest_chapter=2 counts is neither: the licensed title has only three surviving release rows on MU ('v.29.5' by Hi wa Mata Noboru, 'v.1 c.2' by Bonk, 'v.1 c.1' by Gourmet World Scanlation), so the highest chapter number among the records is 2. It is a release-index artifact (G37), like MangaBaka's copied coverage prose - never a chapter count. MU PIN (G56) - MU's 'Vol 29, Chap 263' is OVERSTATED by nine chapters: the anime's furthest first-time coverage is ch 254 (ep 146), and chs 255-263 (Ichiryu's death, the Human World's food collapse, Coco's discovery, Midora's dining table, Toriko's return) are never animated. The pin is also unusable as stored because it lands on eps 145-147, which carry no verifiable manga position - hence G36's refusal. ARC SHAPE - the anime stops mid-Cooking-Festival: the manga's Cooking Festival Arc runs to ch 263, and ch 264 'Now, to Gourmet World!!' opens the Billion Bird Arc (vol 30) and the manga's entire second half, none of which is animated. TYPING SOURCES - AFL's Toriko page gives filler 1, 42-43, 51, 69-70, 80-82, 86, 99, 112-113, 124-125, 130-131, 147; mixed 146; canon everything else including 132-145. ja-WP's 各話リスト bolds anime-original subtitles and bolds exactly the same set MINUS 130, 131 and 147 - 130/131 because ja-WP describes them as the anime dramatising preliminary rounds the manga omitted rather than pure originals, and 147 apparently just never marked (ja-WP's own prose says the anime's endgame 'differs from the source and is original'). The 2011 One Piece crossovers (eps 1 extended, 51, 99) are filler by type and were excluded from the Japanese DVD volumes; they are outside this batch's rows and were not touched. ROW IDENTITY - our 147 rows match ja-WP's 各話リスト and en-WP's 'List of Toriko episodes' one-for-one by title and air date through ep 147 (2014-03-30); there is no recap or special inserted anywhere, so no index shift. Note ja-WP shows the broadcast gap between ep 144 (2014-03-02) and ep 145 (2014-03-16).

flags_for_sean: TERMINAL, split evidence - the one decision in this verdict. Stored/ruled value (2026-08-24) is ep 146 -> ch 253; AFG's Toriko page states 'the last episode that aired is 146 corresponding to Chapter 253... continue from Chapter 254 (Volume 29)'; toriko.fandom's ep-146 chapter field says 253. AGAINST that: ch 253 is entirely the Acacia/Froese flashback ending in Froese's death, and Toei Animation's own synopsis puts that flashback in ep 144, while ep 146's Gourmet-World half is ch 254's content point for point. The fandom fields plateau at 253 across eps 144/145/146, which is the reading-position-header shape. I recommend 254 (with the continue at 255) but the anchor is marked medium because two secondary sources still print 253. If you decline, ep 146 stays 253 / continue 254 and only the ep-145 deletion and the ep-144 continue stand. https://web.archive.org/web/20191110150136/http://www.toei-anim.co.jp/tv/toriko/episode/summary/146/ vs https://www.animefillerguide.com/toriko/

EP 145 TYPE - proposed canon -> filler. AFL types it canon (as part of its 132-145 block) and toriko.fandom prints '253' in its chapter field, so this contradicts two sources; but neither is a content claim, and Toei's official synopsis for the episode contains no manga event. The A44 anchor deletion holds regardless of how you rule the type.
EP 144 TYPE - optional canon -> mixed, offered for completeness, not urged. Half flashback (251-253, canon), half anime-original stadium fight. Declining changes no anchor.

EP 143's {246-247} TAIL is fandom-only. Toei's synopsis for ep 143 shows 243-244 and nothing from the Gourmet World; the only support for 246-247 is the fandom field plus the recap line that opens Toei's ep-144 synopsis. Left as stored; if you want the tighter value it is END 244 {243-244}, which would then make ep 144's START 246 or 247.
EP 144's START 248 is likewise fandom-only - Toei shows the duel beginning and then the Hungry Space wound with almost none of 248-250's fight. Tighter alternative: START 251.

FLAG #695 can be closed as a false positive: MU and AniList are in the same edition; MU's latest_chapter=2 is the highest chapter among three surviving release rows on a licensed title. Consider suppressing latest_chapter as a count signal for licensed/purged MU series generally.
